title: SKU rationalization launch orchestration — release notes cadence, billing cutover, and GTM enablement
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This ticket coordinates the cross-functional launch for the SKU and limits rationalization scheduled for March 2025. Scope covers SKU consolidation, new usage bands and hard limits, billing system mapping, console UI label updates, and all customer/sales-facing communications (release notes, billing comms, and sales enablement).

Objectives:
- Execute a low-risk cutover that preserves invoicing correctness and minimizes customer surprise.
- Ship a clear release notes package and staged comms for affected customers, partners, and internal stakeholders.
- Ensure Sales, Support, and Solutions Engineering have runbooks, objection handling, and migration tools before cutover.
- Monitor key billing and adoption metrics in real time and have rollback/fix-forward remediation ready.

Scope and out-of-scope:
- In-scope: SKU id mapping, entitlement changes, console quota display updates, billing invoice mapping, alerting for customers exceeding new bands, promotional grace periods, and sales enablement collateral.
- Out-of-scope: Engine-side model behavior changes, Dedicated capacity contract re-negotiations (handled by Sales separately).

Stakeholders:
- PM: Aisha Patel (owner)
- Eng: Daniel Morris (assignee) — Billing pipelines and migrations
- Console: Priya Kapoor — UI strings & rollout toggles
- Finance/Billing: Mateo Ruiz — invoice mapping & reconciliation
- Legal & Compliance: Sarah Lin — terms change review
- Sales Enablement: Claire Ng — playbooks & training
- Support: Jamal Owens — runbooks and escalation paths

Rollout plan (high level):
1) Week -3 (now): finalize SKU mapping table + internal PR for billing migration script (GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-migrations/pull/287). Draft release notes and sales one-pager.
2) Week -2: QA migration on staging dataset, reconciliation run against last 2 billing cycles, console UI feature-flag rollout to staging. Run tabletop with Support and Sales.
3) Week -1: Canary cutover for 10% of customers (opt-in from enterprise customers who agreed to beta). Monitor invoice diffs and token accounting for 48 hours.
4) Week 0: Full cutover with staggered waves (region-first: us-west -> us-east -> eu). Post-cutover validation + customer comms.
5) Week +1 to +4: Observability window and follow-up adjustments; mail merges for customers impacted >5% invoice delta.

Release notes cadence and assets to produce:
- Internal embargoed release notes (PM/Eng/Support): confluence draft at https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRIC/pages/sku-rationalization-draft
- Public release notes: one-pager + doc section showing old->new SKU mapping and illustrative invoice examples.
- Billing comms: finance-approved email templates for high-risk customers, including contact & compensation options.
- Changelog snippet for API users: clear examples of SKU names and limits, plus migration hint code.
- Console tooltip copy and FAQ entries.

Sales enablement and support prep:
- 2x 60-minute enablement sessions for AE/SE teams (slides + FAQ doc).
- Objection-handling playbook (price delta, quota changes, credits).
- Migration calculator: lightweight spreadsheet and internal tool to estimate invoice delta (link: drive.google.com/drive/folders/sku-migration-calc).
- Support runbooks: triage steps, how to escalate to Billing SRE, expected SLAs for fixes.

Observability and acceptance criteria:
- Billing reconciliation diff <= 1% for non-edge customers in canary.
- Console quotas reflect new limits within 15 minutes of cutover for >95% of customers.
- No more than 3 P1 billing incidents during first 72 hours post-cutover.
- Customer complaints tracked and categorized; high-severity complaints have response within 4 hours.

Rollback & remediation plan:
- If canary fails (billing diffs > 5% or P1 incidents > 1), automatically revert to previous SKU mapping using feature-flagged migration rollback script (GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-migrations/pull/289).
- For partial discrepancies, run reconciliation job and issue pro-rated credits; Finance to own credit approvals.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Final grace period length for customers migrating across bands (2 weeks suggested, need Finance signoff).
- Whether to force upgrade for legacy SKUs in Console or provide opt-in for 90 days.
- Confirmation from Legal that we can send billing-impact emails without additional consent.

Artifacts & links:
- PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRIC/pages/sku-rationalization-prd
- Migration PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-migrations/pull/287
- Rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-migrations/pull/289
- Release notes draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRIC/pages/sku-rationalization-draft
- Enablement slides (Drive): drive.google.com/sku-enablement-2025

Notes on trade-offs and rationale:
- We prioritize minimal customer accounting delta over aggressive consolidation speed. That means staged waves and conservative default mappings.
- Decision to keep a 2-week grace period balances customer goodwill and Finance reconciliation workload.

Next steps (owner actions):
- [PM] Finalize public release notes and confirm approval with Legal by 2025-02-22.
- [Eng] Complete migration PR review and schedule staging run by 2025-02-24.
- [Finance] Approve credit thresholds and communication templates by 2025-02-25.
- [Sales Enablement] Prepare slides and host first training on 2025-02-26.
comments: 2025-02-11 — Daniel Morris: Began implementation of migration script; running local reconciliation against synthetic dataset. Observed rounding edge case for fractional token credits (tracking in GH issue #94).
2025-02-13 — Claire Ng: Drafted sales FAQs and objection-handling scenarios; requested example invoices for top 10 enterprise customers from Finance.
2025-02-15 — Priya Kapoor: Console tooltip copy ready; will push behind feature flag to staging on 2025-02-17. UI strings PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-ui/pull/712
2025-02-17 — Mateo Ruiz: Finance reconciliation plan approved; need to confirm pro-rated credit thresholds. Will provide sample data by 2025-02-18.
2025-02-19 — Aisha Patel: Updated release notes to include illustrative 'before/after' invoice examples and migration checklist. Legal review scheduled for 2025-02-20.
acceptance_criteria: Migration PR merged and run successfully in staging with diffs < 1% for representative dataset
Public release notes published and slotted into product changelog with embargo lifted at cutover
Sales enablement materials distributed and at least one live training session completed
Support runbooks published and escalation path validated with SRE
